clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old male of African origin presented with a 4-year history of progressive pruritic dermatosis that began as macules and papules on the trunk in 2017 and gradually spread to involve the limbs, buttocks, face, and entire trunk with eventual ulceration. The lesions were initially misdiagnosed and treated as eczema with topical steroids and moisturizing creams from 2017 to 2020 without response. At presentation to ORCI, clinical examination revealed multiple well to ill-defined hyperpigmented erosive plaques, nodules, and tumors occupying >95% of body surface area including non-sun-exposed locations. Skin biopsy confirmed MF with prominent spongiosis, hyperkeratosis, band lymphocytic infiltrate in papillary and reticular dermis, acanthosis, epidermotropism of hyperchromatic lymphocytes with cerebriform nuclei, and occasional Pautrier microabscesses. Immunohistochemistry showed CD3 positivity (CD4, CD5, CD8 not performed). ISCL diagnostic algorithm scoring yielded 6 points (persistent/progressive patches/thin plaques 2 pts, non-sun-exposed location and size/shape variation 2 pts, superficial lymphoid infiltrate 1 pt, lymphocytic atypia 1 pt, CD3+ 1 pt), confirming MF diagnosis. TNM staging was T3N0M0BX (stage 3). Systemic staging workup showed HIV serology negative and normal chest X-ray and abdominal ultrasound. Initial treatment consisted of oral Prednisolone 10 mg twice daily for 30 days and oral Ampiclox 500 mg four times daily for 10 days. The patient achieved remission and at two years post-initial treatment remains in remission on maintenance oral methotrexate 50 mg weekly.
